agentCan: Build the installation URL with a fresh PKCE pair per authorization request
Implement the token exchange, refresh rotation persistence, and invalid_grant-as-uninstall handling
Prepare the Marketplace submission packet (listing content, testing instructions, forms)

approval.cost: No listing/submission fee is stated anywhere in the docs read
approval.trigger: No review is required before real external users can connect: 'Your app does not have to be listed to share and use your installation URL with customers.' The consequence of being unreviewed is a warning: 'Until your app has been reviewed and approved by our team, users will receive an OAuth installation warning that your app has not been reviewed by Klaviyo', though customers can still install and use the app. Marketplace listing is a formal review with an eligibility gate: 'Your app must have at least 5 active customer installs for submission. These must be real customer accounts with live API activity; test accounts do not qualify' (developer accounts or company-associated accounts do not count). Submission (Manage apps > 3 dots > Edit) requires completed Authentication (including testing instructions as a Google Doc with Commenter access adapted from Klaviyo's App & Testing Requirements template), Company details, Listing details, and the Registration & security forms: 'If you submit your application without submitting these forms, your app will be rejected'. Review checks over-scoping explicitly (see Blockers), listing content, testing information, and security (TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest, MFA, logs retained 'a minimum of 365 days'). 'Not all submitted apps will be approved. Klaviyo reserves the right to not list your app for any reason.' Changes to a published app 'will not be published until your app has been re-reviewed and approved'.
approval.wait: Not stated (the docs only say the team 'will follow up via email' if the app is approved, rejected, or needs changes)

blockers.detail: 'You must use the least permissive scope set possible in compliance with our app listing requirements. If your app requests more scope permissions than necessary, it will be rejected.' Scopes are fine-grained resource:action pairs, each endpoint's API reference lists its required scope, and accounts:read is required by default and 'must remain in your scopes list'.
blockers.howToClear: Derive the scope list endpoint-by-endpoint from the API reference and document why each scope is needed in the submission.
blockers.title: Over-scoping is a stated rejection reason

blockers.detail: 'On March 31, 2025, Klaviyo started blocking all OAuth token traffic (oauth/token and oauth/revoke) routed through www.klaviyo.com.' Token traffic must go to a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token and a.klaviyo.com/oauth/revoke; authorize still starts on www.klaviyo.com.
blockers.howToClear: Route authorize and token calls to their different hosts exactly as documented.
blockers.title: Host trap: token traffic moved to a.klaviyo.com

blockers.detail: The 5-install gate must be met with real customer accounts first: you must distribute the unlisted, warning-carrying app to earn eligibility to submit. Testing instructions must follow Klaviyo's template in a shared Google Doc (public documentation links 'will not be accepted'), and you must never share credentials: add integration.directory@klaviyo.com to your test account instead.
blockers.howToClear: Plan a pre-listing distribution phase via the installation URL and instrument install counts from launch.
blockers.title: Listing eligibility is a chicken-and-egg gate

alternatives: Private API keys (per-account credentials for your own/single-account integrations; Klaviyo pushes OAuth for anything distributed, and key-based apps had to migrate: 'If your app uses private key authentication, you'll need to update your app to OAuth by June 30th, 2025... Failure to update may cause service disruptions and potential de-listing')
flavor.recommended: A public OAuth app using the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), token exchange done server-to-server
flavor.why: The object is an app created on the Manage apps page (klaviyo.com/manage-apps) via Create app, issuing a client ID and client secret. 'Klaviyo requires PKCE for safely storing credentials for both public and confidential client types.' Tokens are account-scoped, not user-scoped: 'Access tokens and refresh tokens grant access to Klaviyo accounts, not users', so agencies/platforms connect each Klaviyo account separately. 'Public apps that can be installed from Klaviyo's App Marketplace require authentication via OAuth.'

humanMust: Create the app (only owner, admin, and manager roles can create OAuth apps in Klaviyo) and securely save the client secret ('You won't be able to view your client secret again, although you can generate a new one later')
Set the scopes and Redirect URLs in the UI and Save
Distribute the installation URL; after 5+ real installs, complete the Marketplace submission including the Registration & security forms
name: Klaviyo
nuances: Refresh semantics are unusual: refreshing issues a new access token but 'the previous access token is not revoked. The access token remains valid until it expires or the user uninstalls the app'; refresh tokens rotate on every use, so persist the latest after every refresh. Refresh tokens remain valid until the app is uninstalled, except: 'If a refresh token is not used after 90 days, it is revoked', and refresh can be called at most 10 times per minute.

invalid_grant on refresh (400) means treat as uninstalled: 'You can treat all invalid_grant responses, regardless of the error_description, like the application has been uninstalled by the user' (causes include uninstall, 90-day no-use expiry, and Klaviyo security revocation).

Access tokens cannot be revoked: 'The revoke endpoint only accepts refresh tokens. Access tokens are JWTs that are intended to be short-lived.' Access tokens are valid for 1 hour ('this is subject to change'); authorization codes expire in 5 minutes. Access tokens may be up to 4,096 characters and refresh tokens 512 characters.
'OAuth apps receive their own rate limit quota per installed app instance (i.e., per account per app)', unlike private keys which share a per-account quota.

Token exchange must be server-to-server ('The client secret is private and should never be in the browser') and form-encoded: sending JSON 'can result in difficult to debug errors'. The redirect_uri must exactly match the allowlist, and 'your OAuth app must be able to support installation from both klaviyo.com and any subdomain of klaviyo.com'. Generate a new code_challenge/code_verifier pair for every unique authorization request and store the verifier keyed by a customer identifier passed as state.
prerequisites: A Klaviyo account with owner, admin, or manager role (only those roles can create OAuth apps)
The minimum scope set (accounts:read is mandatory) derived from the API reference

steps.detail: Manage apps > Create app > name it > 'securely save your client secret and client ID. You won't be able to view your client secret again' > Create.
steps.title: Create the app

steps.detail: Set the space-separated scope list ('you must use the least permissive scope set possible'; accounts:read is required and must remain) and the Redirect URLs allowlist (multiple URLs separated by space/tab/enter). Save.
steps.title: Set scopes and Redirect URLs

steps.detail: www.klaviyo.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=...&state=...&code_challenge_method=S256&code_challenge=... Generate a new PKCE pair for every unique authorization request and store the code_verifier server-side keyed by a customer identifier passed as state. On approval Klaviyo redirects with code and state; on denial with error=access_denied. The code expires in 5 minutes.
steps.title: Build the installation URL (fresh PKCE per request)

steps.detail: POST a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token with Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret) and a form-encoded body (grant_type=authorization_code, code, code_verifier, redirect_uri). Store access_token, refresh_token, expires_in (1 hour), scope. Call the API with Authorization: Bearer; reuse the access token for its whole lifetime.
steps.title: Exchange the code (note the a.klaviyo.com host)

steps.detail: POST the token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token; persist the newly returned token set (refresh tokens rotate). On uninstall, POST a.klaviyo.com/oauth/revoke with the refresh token. Treat any invalid_grant on refresh as an uninstall.
steps.title: Refresh (rotating) and revoke on uninstall

steps.detail: Share the installation URL with customers immediately (unreviewed apps carry an installation warning but work). After at least 5 active customer installs with live API activity, optionally submit for Marketplace review via Manage apps > 3 dots > Edit: Authentication (with template-based testing instructions), Company details, Listing details, and the Registration & security forms, then Review submission > Submit.
steps.title: Distribute now; submit for listing at 5 installs

tagline: Self-serve OAuth with mandatory PKCE and account-scoped tokens: real customers can install from your own URL today (with an 'unreviewed' warning), while the App Marketplace review is optional but gated behind 5 active customer installs and rejects over-scoped apps on sight.

time.active: ~15 min of app setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day to distribute; Marketplace review duration not stated
